packs.title: Racing, Art and Discovery
packs.promise: Explore Indianapolis through racing stories, museums, canal views and a renewed industrial district.

q.t: A Line from Art to Paper
q.s: Use one visual relationship to begin your own work.
st: Choose an artwork in an open gallery and credit its maker and title.
Notice the relationship between a line and an area of color.
Create an original small composition or written scene using a different subject.

q.s: Use a habitat label to distinguish facts from guesses.
st: Choose an open habitat and read its interpretation.
Find two stated details about the animal’s needs or care.
Write the details with their source and one question you still have.

q.s: Respond to an artist’s material choice with your own idea.
st: Choose an artwork and record the artist, title and label-stated material.
Notice one visual quality of that material without touching the work.
Using pencil or writing afterward, imagine a different original object using that quality; do not reproduce cultural motifs.

packs.title: Water, Stone, Shade
packs.promise: Follow small details around the canal and river.

q.s: Collect three details at the park entrance.
st: From an open path, find a branch shape, a patch of light or shade, and one paving texture.
Describe each in one or two words. Bare branches and overcast light count.
Keep planted areas untouched and record your trio.

q.s: Find three ways stone shapes a path.
st: Use the open promenade and find a smooth stone face, a joint and a carved or contrasting detail.
If a carving is not visible, choose a second texture instead.
Record the three finds without rubbing, climbing or touching the stone.

q.s: Notice a tree in any season.
st: From the public path, choose one tree and notice a branching direction, a light or dark patch, and a shape near its base.
Leaves and flowers are optional; do not identify a species from guesswork.
Record the three features without touching or collecting anything.
